2. Brief facts of the case is that, the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 in the said Court for declaration that the impugned auction sale described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint is illegal, void, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiff opposite party No. 1 filed the suit being Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 alleging, in short, inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Bani Amin and Arab Ali, the predecessors who were the recorded tenants of CS khatian, that during the revisional settlement operation the said land was wrongly recorded in the name of Late Wazed Ali Zamaddar, predecessor of the defendant, hence the plaintiff-opposite-party filed Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 before the Assistant Judge, Barguna for declaration of their title in the suit land. It was further stated in the plaint that the said Bani Amin and Arab Ali had their dwelling houses, etc. in the suit land appertaining to PS khatian No. 59 measuring an area of 12.86 but only 0.62 decimals of land was recorded in RS Khatian in the name of Bani Amin. In Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 the present petitioner was a defendant along with his brother Mahabubul Haque and others being the heirs of Late Wazed Ali Zamaddar, the said defendants filed written statements in the said Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 contending, inter alia, that their father Late Wazed Ali auction purchased the suit land in Money Suit No, 5 of 1932, vide Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 of the 1st Court of Munsif, Pirojpur and took possession on 20-2-1934 and since then was in possession of the same. The further case of the plaintiff-opposite-party No. 1 is that, the aforesaid Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 was dismissed on contest and he pursued the matter unsuccessfully up to the Appellate Di vision. The further case of the plaintiff-opposite-party No. 1 in the present suit is that, the Bainanama and Dakhalnama vide Exhibits. A and D filed by the defendants in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 in the trial Court were taken back by them on 23-7-86 on application and certified copies of the same were refiled before the High Court Division long after more than 8 years in Civil Revision No. 732 of 1990, filed by the plaintiff opposite party instead of original Exhibits A and B filed and taken back as aforesaid. The plaintiff further alleged that the learned District Judges having not been in seisin of the said Exhibits A and B, could not properly adjudicate the matter. The defendants filed the certified copies of Exhibits. A and B before the High Court Division only on 2-11-94 in said Civil Revision No. 732 of 1990, the High Court Division discharged the Rule vide its judgment and order dated 31-1-95 and the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 thus did not get sufficient time to verify those copies. The plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 further stated in his plaint of the present suit that, after obtaining certified copies of Bainanama and Dakhalnama of the aforesaid Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 on 11-8-97, he found that the certified copies of the Exhibits. A and B filed before the Hon'ble High Court Di vision on 2-11-1994 were forged, fabricated and false and on consideration of the said fake documents, the superior Courts ultimately dismissed his suit. The plaintiff further alleged that after obtaining the certified copies of the Bainanama and Dakhalnama of Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 he came to certified copies before the Appellate Division in a know of the said fraud on 11-8-97 and filed the said separate paper book at the time of hearing of the leave petition, but the Hon'ble Appellate Division has neither referred the said Paper Book nor discussed or gave any findings on those papers in its judgment and order dated 21-8-97 rejecting the Leave Petition. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances the plaintiff-opposite party instituted the present suit as aforesaid. 

 3. The defendant-petitioner appeared in the, suit and filed an application under Order 7, rule 11(a) and (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting the plaint pleading that the suit is barred by limitation and rule of res judicata alleging that, the plaintiff having instituted the present suit for declaration that the Bainanama and Dakhalnami of Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 as described in schedule Ka of the plaint are forged, collusive, ineffective, inoperative, non-existent, baseless and not binding upon the plaintiff is not maintainable in this subsequent suit as it is barred by limitation as well as by their principle of res judicata under section 11 of the Code alleging the, that plaintiff-opposite-party had already instituted Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 on the same facts and the defendant Nos. 3 and 10 of that suit including the petitioner, filed a written statement on 23-7-1986 contesting the suit. The petitioner further alleged in the application that, in the said written statements they stated the case of auction sale in Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 in question and produced the Bainanama and Dakhalnama of the case in the said suit which were duly marked as Exts. A and B at the time of trial and as such the plaintiff 'had clear knowledge of the aforesaid Bainanama and Dakhalnama at least from the date of filing of their written statements, that is, from 23-7- 86, but the present suit having not been filed within 6 years from 23-7-86, the suit is barred by limitation and, as such, the plaint is liable to be rejected. 

 8. Elucidating his first submission Mr. Abdul Quayum submits that, even if we accept that the plaintiff had no knowledge of the spurious Bainanama and Dakhalnama earlier, it can definitely be pleaded that he had definite knowledge of the same at least when the fact of aforesaid auction sale in Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 4 of 1933 were disclosed in the written statements filed on 23-7-86 in Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 and were produced in Court and admitted into evidence and marked as Exhibits A and B during trial of the suit in 1986. So, the suit having been filed in 1988 referring the same facts and challenging the said Bainanama and Dakhalnama, the present suit is clearly barred by law of limitation and the trial Court ought to have rejected the plaint. He further submits that the trial Court ought to have found that the plaintiffs claim that, he came to know that Exhibits A and B were forged, false and fabricated documents only on 11-8-97 after obtaining the certified copies of the said documents is not true and correct 

 14. On the second leg of his submission, Mr Quayum vigorously argued that, the plaint ought to have been rejected by the trial Court finding that the same is barred by section 11 of the Code, that is, barred by the rule of res judicata. The learned Advocate submits that the fact and issue involved in the present suit have been directly and substantially in issue in the former suit between the same parties. He submits that if it appears from the reading of the plaint itself that the facts and issues involved in the suit were directly and substantially in issue in the former suit, the subsequent suit is not maintainable under the provisions of section 11 of the Code being barred by principle of res judicata. In elaborating his submission the learned Advocate took me to the averments made in the plaint and read out different paragraph of the same. It appears from the plaint at the present Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 that, there has been statements of some facts of the former suit being Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 on aforesaid auction sale, Bainanama, dakhalnama, etc in connection with Rent Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933, etc. In view of such statements made in the plaint by the plaintiff, which have already been decided and disposed of in the former suit between the parties, the learned Advocate submits that, those cannot be tried in the subsequent suit as per provision of section 11 of the Code and so the plaint is liable to be rejected outright without going into evidence. In support of his submission he referred a decision of a case between Sreemati Pushpa Rani Das and another vs AKM Habibur Rahman and others, reported in 13 BLD (AD) 217. He also referred to decisions of the cases between Guinness Peat (Trading) Limited vs Md Fazlur Rahman, reported in 44 DLR (AD) 242, Shafiq Ahmed vs Mirza Muhammad Anwar Geb, reported in 20 DLR (WP) 113 and in the case between Habibullah and others vs SA Mujtaba and others, reported in 34 DLR 418.
